papers.title: Evolution of Food Science: Bridging Tradition and Innovation
papers.abstract: Food science has evolved from indigenous culinary wisdom and ancient preservation methods into a complex interdisciplinary field that integrates modern technological advancements, systems biology, and data analytics. This transformation reflects a continuous interplay between traditional knowledge systems and cutting-edge scientific innovation aimed at addressing contemporary global challenges including nutrition security, public health, and environmental sustainability. This chapter comprehensively examines the historical foundations of food science, its scientific milestones, and contemporary innovations such as biotechnology, nanotechnology, and personalized nutrition. Further, it highlights integrative approaches that meld traditional practices with novel technologies, supported by illustrative case studies. Ethical considerations surrounding intellectual property and cultural stewardship are discussed alongside future directions emphasizing systems thinking, resilience, and equity. This synthesis articulates a pathway toward sustainable, ethical, and health-promoting food systems at the nexus of tradition and innovation. Keywords: food science, traditional knowledge, food innovation, biotechnology, functional foods, nutrigenomics, sustainability, food safety, culinary heritage
papers.venue: International Journal of Research and Review

papers.title: Modification of the Proximity Indexed Value Method Based on Distance-Based Normalization to Improve the Stability of Alternative Rankings
papers.abstract: The Proximity Indexed Value (PIV) method provides a proximity-based mechanism for ranking alternatives in multi-criteria decision-making; however, its ranking results can be affected by the normalization process and the relative characteristics of criterion values. This study proposes a Distance-Based Proximity Indexed Value (D-PIV) method by incorporating distance-based normalization into the PIV framework to represent the proximity of alternatives to criterion-specific ideal conditions more explicitly. The proposed method was evaluated using an alternative location selection dataset comprising eight alternatives and six criteria, including one cost criterion and five benefit criteria. The evaluation included comparative ranking analysis using 36 systematic criterion-weight perturbation scenarios with changes of ±0.05, ±0.10, and ±0.15. The results show that D-PIV changes the ordering of Loc 3 and Loc 8 compared with conventional PIV, resulting in a ranking that fully corresponds to the reference ranking. The Spearman correlation increased from 0.9762 for PIV to 1.0000 for D-PIV. However, the sensitivity analysis indicates that the distance-based modification does not uniformly improve ranking stability across all alternatives. D-PIV increases the stability of Loc 8 from 69.44% to 72.22%, while lower stability is observed for Loc 3 and Loc 6 compared with PIV. These findings demonstrate that D-PIV contributes a reference-oriented normalization mechanism that improves baseline ranking consistency while redistributing, rather than uniformly eliminating, sensitivity to criterion-weight variations. The study therefore provides both a methodological contribution through the integration of distance-based normalization into PIV and an empirical contribution through systematic evidence of its effects on ranking agreement and stability.
papers.venue: Journal of Decision Support Systems and Multi-Criteria Decision Making

papers.title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
papers.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.
papers.venue: Galore International Journal of Health Sciences and Research

papers.title: The Impact of Digital Literacy-Based Assignments on Students’ Mastery of Islamic Education and Learning Habits: A Multivariate Regression Analysis
papers.abstract: ENGLISH: The Impact of Digital Literacy-Based Assignments on Students’ Mastery of Islamic Education and Learning Habits: A Multivariate Regression AnalysisObjective: This study aims to analyze the simultaneous effects of digital literacy assignments on the mastery of Islamic Education material on the theme of tolerance and learning habits of eighth-grade students at SMPN 08 Lebong. Method: This study uses a quantitative approach with survey methods and multivariate regression analysis to test the relationship between digital literacy, mastery of material, and learning habits. Results: Digital literacy-based assignments significantly influence both variables, contributing 42.8% to mastery of the material and 13.2% to learning habits. Conclusion: Digital literacy effectively improves mastery of Islamic Education material, but its influence on learning habits still requires support from other holistic strategies. Contribution: This study suggests that digital assignments should emphasize the learning habit formation process and the reinforcement of Islamic character values. These findings contribute to developing technology-based curricula relevant to Islamic education in the digital age.INDONESIAN: Pengaruh Penugasan Melalui Literasi Digital terhadap Penguasaan Materi PAI Tema Toleransi dan Kebiasaan Belajar Siswa: Analisis Regresi MultivariatTujuan: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh penugasan melalui literasi digital terhadap penguasaan materi Pendidikan Agama Islam (PAI) tema toleransi dan kebiasaan belajar siswa kelas VIII SMPN 08 Lebong secara simultan. Metode: Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei dan analisis regresi multivariat untuk menguji hubungan antara variabel literasi digital, penguasaan materi, dan kebiasaan belajar. Hasil: Penugasan berbasis literasi digital memberikan pengaruh signifikan terhadap kedua variabel, dengan kontribusi sebesar 42,8% terhadap penguasaan materi dan 13,2% terhadap kebiasaan belajar. Kesimpulan: Literasi digital efektif dalam meningkatkan penguasaan materi PAI, namun pengaruhnya terhadap kebiasaan belajar masih memerlukan dukungan strategi lain yang lebih holistik. Kontribusi: Penelitian ini menyarankan agar penugasan digital didesain dengan penekanan pada proses pembiasaan belajar dan penguatan nilai-nilai karakter Islami. Temuan ini memberikan kontribusi penting bagi pengembangan kurikulum berbasis teknologi yang relevan dengan pendidikan Islam di era digital.

papers.title: “Calcare Cavernoso” as a key predisposing factor for sinkhole occurrence in Tuscany (Italy): inventory update, remote sensing detection, and GIS–ML susceptibility modelling
papers.abstract: The “Calcare Cavernoso” (cavernous limestone) formation is a dolomitic carbonate unit characterized by a vacuolar texture and high intrinsic porosity, which favours groundwater-driven dissolution and cavity development and may predispose to subsidence. This study investigates the spatial relationship between sinkholes and the distribution of “Calcare Cavernoso” in Tuscany (Italy) and updates the regional subset of the ISPRA national sinkhole database. An integrated approach combined bibliographic information, targeted field surveys, historical cartography, and multi-source geospatial datasets. Geological and thematic layers were retrieved from the Tuscany “Geoscopio” portal, while Copernicus Sentinel-2 imagery was processed using the Normalized Difference Water Index (NDWI) to support the detection of flooded sinkholes. Historical maps were exploited to infer sinkhole persistence and potential evolutionary trends, including partial or complete infilling. All thematic layers (geology, faults, hydrography, quarries, mines, topography, and sinkholes) were harmonized, georeferenced, and rasterized on a 250 × 250 m grid within an ESRI ArcGIS environment. Susceptibility modelling was implemented using density-based proxies and an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) framework, producing probability outputs subsequently grouped into classes to enhance operational usability. The results substantially expand the regional sinkhole inventory (from 88 to 1223 mapped features) and support a strong spatial association between sinkhole occurrence and “Calcare Cavernoso”, further corroborated by targeted field checks. The most influential susceptibility drivers include “Calcare Cavernoso”, low-slope settings, DTM-derived parameters, fault density, and anthropogenic underground activities (quarries and mines), while other variables show secondary or more complex contributions.

papers.title: Anthropogenic sinkholes in the urban fabric of Messina (Sicily, Italy)
papers.abstract: Urban anthropogenic sinkholes are increasingly reported in Messina (Sicily, Italy), where culverted torrents, legacy underground works, and dense utilities intersect a Holocene coastal/alluvial plain. We present an updated, georeferenced inventory of sinkholes within the municipal urban area, built from local press/ web sources and field cross-checks, and we assess spatial relationships with culverted drainage and known urban cavity entrances. To frame site-effects in a seismic setting, we consult the Italian catalogue of earthquake-induced ground failures (CEDIT) and the Italian catalogue of earthquake environmental effects (EEE), which document widespread ground cracking, settlement and liquefaction during major historical earthquakes, notably the 1908 Messina event. Our results highlight clusters along culverted stream corridors and in zones influenced by underground legacy, supporting future scenario-based prioritization of inspections and post-event checks.

papers.title: Mapping natural sinkhole susceptibility in Italy: integrating a national inventory with machine learning
papers.abstract: Natural sinkholes are a widespread geohazard in Italy, complicating landuse planning and risk reduction. This study develops the first national-scale susceptibility map for natural sinkholes using an updated inventory and data-driven modelling. Building on the ISPRA National Sinkhole Database, we assembled more than 14,000 documented features from literature, historical records, imagery and regional datasets. Geological, geomorphological, structural, hydrogeological and geochemical factors were converted into gridded predictors and combined with the inventory through a machine-learning regression framework estimating a continuous susceptibility score. The calibrated model, evaluated on a held-out 20% test subset, produces a susceptibility surface for the Italian territory. Interpretation tools emphasize the importance of soluble rocks, fault-controlled permeability, deep gas emissions and mineralized springs, consistent with previous studies. High-susceptibility zones align with major karst and evaporitic provinces, including the Friuli-Veneto piedmont, northern Apulia, Latium travertine basins and central Sicilian evaporites, whereas western Alpine sectors and Sardinia show very low scores. The map offers a coherent national overview of where natural sinkholes are more likely to occur and provides an operational basis for prioritizing surveys, monitoring programmes and planning measures, while the methodology can be refined to incorporate time-dependent drivers and multi-hazard interactions. These advances support more resilient and sustainable territorial development.

papers.title: Using Photography as a Tool for Critical Urban Diagnosis: An Undomestication Strategy
papers.abstract: This research describes a teaching experience of urbanism using photography as a critical pedagogical strategy of educating the look to raise awareness among undergraduate students about the problems of their context, employing the objective worldview of each participant regarding their perception of the city and understanding their role as knowledge builders.This was a descriptive field research, based on participant observation methodology, structured in four stages, through a process of categorizing photographs taken by the attendees, shaping positive and negative aspects of the experience.Information obtained was correlated on a database for visualizing the study data through opensource software, with the final identification of the main phenomena.Through this process, a significant disparity was detected in the perception of the observers; therefore, the importance of promoting other educational practices that can raise awareness among architecture and urbanism students about the different urban singularities present in the built environment of developing countries.
